note: Rehearsal callers for staff (and the agent itself). Difficulty 1-5. Score each run: disclosure said, details captured (name/number/address/issue), emergency flagged correctly, range quoted not invented, no card details taken, callback promise set.

scenarios.title: Dripping tap, daytime price-shopper
scenarios.caller: Calm homeowner, wants a price for a dripping kitchen tap, weekday morning.
scenarios.pass: Standard intake complete, range quoted, callback promised.

scenarios.title: Boiler dead, Friday 7pm, family with kids
scenarios.caller: Cold house, two small children, wants to know if someone comes tonight and what it costs.
beats: classify: heating failure with children = EMERGENCY in winter
traps: downgrading to standard because caller is polite
scenarios.pass: Emergency flagged, owner SMS queued, caller told exactly what happens next.

scenarios.title: Burst pipe, 2am, water through ceiling
scenarios.caller: Panicking, water pouring, doesn't know where the stopcock is.
beats: stopcock instruction FIRST (under kitchen sink, then boiler off)
overnight range stated, confirm on arrival
traps: taking details before stopping the water
scenarios.pass: Damage-control advice given before admin, emergency escalated.

scenarios.title: Angry repeat caller, still waiting from Tuesday
scenarios.caller: Furious, booked Tuesday, nobody came, demands compensation and the owner's mobile number.
beats: acknowledge + take details, do NOT hand out owner number
escalate as priority callback + owner SMS noting complaint
scenarios.pass: De-escalated, details captured, owner notified, nothing promised that isn't policy.

scenarios.title: Elderly caller, no heating, confused about address
scenarios.caller: 88 years old, cold, unsure of postcode, repeats herself, mentions a care visitor in the morning.
beats: reassure: help tonight, care visitor told in morning digest
scenarios.pass: Vulnerability flagged, help arranged tonight, dignity intact.
